passages.title: Planning advertisements by issue
body: Velnari Trade Review publishes four seasonal issues for independent shop owners. An issue's cover month identifies the season it discusses; it is not the month in which copies leave our mailing room. Advertisers should therefore use the dispatch calendar when planning an offer that begins on a particular date. Our readers often keep an issue beside their ordering desk for several weeks.
The March issue leaves on February 12, the June issue on May 14, the September issue on August 13, and the December issue on November 12. Artwork is due fourteen days before dispatch.
Each issue accepts both full-page and half-page advertisements, and neither format receives priority in the production schedule. A proof is sent to the named contact before printing.

Advertisers may include a short web address, but we cannot change a printed address after approval. Extra copies can be purchased separately. The editorial office handles articles; advertising files and proof corrections belong with the production desk.

passages.title: Our advertising booking
heading: To: Production desk
From: Mira Delven
Subject: Our first booking
body: We would like our first advertisement to appear in the issue mailed during August. Our autumn wholesale collection reaches shops in early September, and buyers need some time to compare the colors before placing their initial orders. The advertisement will show six products together rather than one large photograph of our most expensive item.

Please reserve a half page. Our designer has supplied a draft with a short address leading directly to the wholesale collection. I will review the proof myself while our sales director is away. I am also arranging copies for four representatives who do not receive the magazine through its regular mailing list. The product descriptions are finished, but the photographs still need approval from our merchandising team. They meet on July 22. I can send the completed artwork on July 26. Please send the advertising invoice to our accounts assistant, who has a different email address from mine.

body: 벨나리 무역 리뷰는 독립 점주를 위해 계절호 네 개를 발행한다. 표지 월은 다루는 계절이며 우편 발송 월이 아니다. 특정 날짜에 시작하는 행사를 기획할 때는 발송 일정을 사용해야 한다. 독자들은 주문 책상 옆에 잡지를 몇 주씩 두곤 한다.

모든 호에 전면과 반면 광고가 가능하며 크기에 따른 제작 우선권은 없다. 인쇄 전 지정 담당자에게 교정본을 보낸다.
짧은 웹 주소를 넣을 수 있지만 승인 후 인쇄된 주소는 바꿀 수 없다. 추가 부수는 별도 구매할 수 있다. 기사는 편집실에서, 광고 파일과 교정은 제작 담당 부서에서 처리한다.

passages.title: Color continuity in woven fabric
body: At Neralvi Textiles, fabric is dyed in batches large enough to fill several rolls. Two rolls can carry the same color name yet show a slight difference when placed side by side. For uninterrupted wall coverings, buyers generally choose rolls from one dye batch. A printed color name identifies the recipe, while the batch reference identifies a single production run.

The mill keeps a small cutting from every batch for comparison. These retained pieces are stored away from daylight because exposure can change their appearance. Customers should also compare cuttings with their selvage edges aligned. Reversing one length can make its weave reflect light differently, even when both lengths come from the same batch. The latest dispatch summary identifies rolls Alder and Birch as batch D31, Cedar and Willow as D32. All four are described as Mist Gray. The summary gives roll identities separately from the dimensions printed on the shipping sleeves; roll names do not indicate length. Buyers can obtain the full production certificate from the customer service team.

passages.title: Fabric received at the design studio
heading: To: Project team
From: Oren Savel
Subject: Reception project materials
body: We unwrapped the four rolls for the Rellova reception project this morning. Alder contains eighteen meters, Birch twelve, Cedar ten, and Willow fourteen. Our installer needs twenty-six meters for the continuous wall behind the reception counter. She can join two lengths behind a vertical trim strip, where the seam will not be visible.

The rolls arrived in good condition, and we have kept the shipping sleeves beside them. A representative from the mill is visiting on Thursday afternoon. Our installation planner will bring scaled drawings of the trim strips so the team can agree where the seams will be hidden. The wall itself has been measured twice, and no extra length is needed beyond the twenty-six meters already stated.
There is also a separate display panel in another room. We have not yet decided what fabric to use there.
I have asked the installer to leave the cutting until after Thursday's discussion and to photograph the labels before removing the sleeves.

passagesKo.title: 직물의 색상 연속성
body: 네랄비 직물은 여러 롤을 채울 양을 한 번에 염색한다. 같은 색상 이름이라도 나란히 놓으면 약간 다를 수 있다. 이어지는 벽면에는 보통 같은 염색 배치의 롤을 선택한다. 색상명은 배합을, 배치 번호는 한 번의 생산을 나타낸다.

공장은 비교용으로 각 배치의 작은 조각을 보관한다. 햇빛으로 외관이 달라질 수 있어 차광 보관한다. 고객은 직물의 가장자리 방향을 맞추어 견본을 비교해야 한다. 같은 배치라도 한 조각의 방향을 뒤집으면 직조 무늬가 빛을 다르게 반사할 수 있다. 최근 발송 요약에 따르면 Alder와 Birch는 D31, Cedar와 Willow는 D32이다. 네 롤 모두 Mist Gray라고 표시돼 있다. 롤 이름은 길이를 나타내지 않으며 치수는 포장 슬리브에 별도로 기재한다. 전체 생산 증명서는 고객 서비스팀에 요청할 수 있다.

passages.title: Understanding marketplace visibility
body: Vesnali Market gives business sellers two separate reports about how visitors discover their products. The search report counts visits from unpaid results, while the sponsored-placement report counts visits from advertisements. A product can appear in both places during the same week. The reports help sellers distinguish traffic earned through a listing from traffic purchased through a campaign.

A visit is counted when someone opens the product page, not when a product merely appears on a screen. Purchases are reported separately. More visits therefore do not necessarily mean more sales. Sellers comparing weeks should check that both reports cover the same number of days.

A free listing consultation is available. An adviser examines photographs, descriptions, and category choices but cannot guarantee a particular search position. Sellers bring their own reports, which remain confidential and are not shown to other businesses.

passages.title: Weekly seller dashboard
body: The table records visits during June 2–8. Both source reports were exported together, and their dates were checked before the figures were copied into this summary. The entries concern product-page visits, not appearances in search results. The dashboard contains no figures for canceled orders.

Each product was available throughout the seven days. No listing was paused, and no entry includes the following week's visits. Someone who opened a page through different sources on different occasions can contribute to both reports. These are visit counts rather than counts of distinct people.

The seller exported the dashboard on June 10. Purchase quantities are held in another report managed by the order team. All four trays use the same package size but have different surface finishes. The export contains no information about visitors' occupations or their employers.

I also photographed the tray described in our catalog as smooth charcoal. That is Flint. Fern is pale green, Reed is natural brown, and Moss is dark green. The pictures show the products from above and from the side, with a ruler beside each one.

The consultation is on June 14. I will bring the original image files on a portable drive because the adviser may want to enlarge them. Our warehouse assistant took all the photographs in daylight, and no colors have been digitally altered.

passagesKo.title: 온라인 장터 노출
body: 베스날리 마켓은 상품 발견 경로를 두 보고서로 제공한다. 검색 보고서는 무료 결과 방문, 광고 보고서는 광고 방문이다. 같은 주에 한 상품이 양쪽에 나타날 수 있다. 상품 정보로 얻은 방문과 캠페인으로 구입한 방문을 구별한다.
상품이 화면에 보일 때가 아니라 페이지를 열 때 센다. 구매는 별도이므로 방문 증가가 판매 증가를 뜻하지 않는다. 주간 비교 때는 기간의 일수가 같은지 확인해야 한다.
무료 상담에서 사진·설명·분류를 살피지만 특정 검색 순위는 보장하지 못한다. 판매자가 가져온 보고서는 비밀이며 다른 업체에 보여 주지 않는다.

body: 표는6월2~8일 방문이다. 두 출처 보고서를 함께 내보내고 날짜를 확인해 옮겼다. 검색 결과 표시가 아닌 상품 페이지 방문이며 취소 주문 수치는 없다.

passages.title: Comparing press interruptions
body: Rovekna Stampings is studying interruptions on its small metal presses. The production sheet gives total minutes when each press was not producing, including scheduled cleaning and unexpected interruptions. Analysts subtract scheduled cleaning to compare unexpected downtime. Otherwise, a machine with a thorough cleaning routine might appear less reliable than it is.

The comparison concerns duration rather than event frequency. A single long stoppage can matter more than several brief ones. Operators must nevertheless record each event separately because maintenance staff need descriptions when investigating causes. The production office combines the times only for the weekly summary. This trial uses machines that make the same simple bracket and have equal scheduled operating hours. Material supply was continuous. Product quality is checked by another team and is not part of this comparison. The manager wants a chart that clearly distinguishes these different aspects of production performance.

passages.title: Wednesday production sheet
body: Total nonproducing time: Amber press 65 minutes; Cobalt press 50 minutes; Garnet press 80 minutes; Ivory press 55 minutes. Every total includes the operator's scheduled cleaning entry. The supervisor checked start and finish times against the wall clock before signing the sheet.

The maintenance notebook describes the longest unexpected event on each press: Amber had a loose feed guide; Cobalt had a worn belt; Garnet had a blocked discharge chute; Ivory had an intermittent foot switch. These descriptions identify events rather than giving the total time lost on each machine.

The trial ran from eight until four. The same batch of metal supplied all four presses. Operators placed completed brackets in separate containers so that inspectors could later examine each machine's output without confusing the sources.

passages.title: Trial cleaning entries
heading: To: Production analyst
From: Sera Nolven
Subject: Trial notes
body: Wednesday's planned cleaning periods were Amber twenty minutes, Cobalt ten, Garnet forty, and Ivory twenty-five. I confirmed these figures with the operators. There were no other scheduled nonproduction periods, and all these entries are already included in the production sheet's totals.
The maintenance manager wants to investigate the press with the greatest unexpected downtime first. Please keep machine names visible in the comparison.
The notebook descriptions came from operators who were present during the events, so the manager can approach them for further information.

I also collected photographs taken at the start of cleaning. They show the work surfaces, not the finished brackets. The images are in the shared trial folder. The inspection team's separate quality report will arrive next week after dimensional measurements are complete. Until then, the brackets remain in their labeled containers.

body: 로베크나 금속은 소형 프레스 중단을 조사한다. 생산표 총 비생산 시간에는 예정 청소와 돌발 중단이 포함된다. 돌발 정지를 비교하려면 청소 시간을 뺀다. 그렇지 않으면 철저히 청소한 기계가 덜 신뢰할 만해 보일 수 있다.
비교는 횟수가 아닌 기간이다. 짧은 여러 번보다 한 번의 긴 정지가 중요할 수 있다. 정비 원인 조사에는 설명이 필요하므로 사건은 각각 기록하고 주간 요약에서만 합친다. 같은 브래킷과 같은 예정 가동 시간으로 시험하며 자재는 계속 공급됐다. 별도 팀의 품질 검사는 이 비교 대상이 아니다. 관리자는 생산 성과의 서로 다른 측면이 구별되는 차트를 원한다.

passages.title: A proposed advertising exchange
body: Telsavi Instruments would like to exchange advertising space with your publishing company. We publish a quarterly bulletin for laboratory purchasing managers. Each issue contains a page introducing outside services. We do not accept money for that page; participating publishers instead provide space for our instrument advertisement in their own publications.

We are considering an autumn exchange. Our team can supply either a full-page vertical design or a half-page horizontal design. A narrow strip would make the instrument diagrams too small, so that format is unsuitable. The diagrams must remain beside the operating specifications to be useful to readers.

Please send the available formats and the number of copies mailed directly to purchasing departments. Total circulation alone does not show how many intended readers we would reach. We want a title sending more than three thousand copies to those departments. Your information will be reviewed at our next editorial meeting.

passages.title: Publishing portfolio
body: Varenvi Publishing offers four business titles. Benchline circulates 8,000 copies, with 40 percent mailed to purchasing departments. Assay World circulates 6,000, with half sent to those departments. Instrument Ledger circulates 10,000, with a purchasing-department share of 35 percent. Lab Window sends 70 percent of its 5,000 copies to purchasing departments.

Remaining copies go to technical employees, educators, and service organizations. These readers receive identical editorial pages and advertisements. Percentages reflect mailing lists reviewed in July. Exhibition copies are not included in the circulation figures, since they are picked up by visitors whose occupations are not recorded. All four titles commission independent writers. Advertisements are marked clearly and kept separate from editorial recommendations. A publisher exchanging space receives an issue after mailing, together with a page image for its internal records. The exchange itself does not include any promise of editorial coverage.

heading: To: Telsavi Instruments

body: Our autumn plans are now firm. Benchline has a horizontal half page available. Assay World has a vertical full page. Instrument Ledger and Lab Window each have only a narrow horizontal strip. The page widths for all titles appear in the attachment.

The Benchline editor mentioned a winter feature about purchasing measurement equipment. Assay World is preparing a profile of a laboratory designer. These articles are being handled independently of advertising. I have included editorial contacts in case your technical team wants to provide background information.

Please send a name for the exchange correspondence. The proof contact need not be the person negotiating the arrangement. Our production coordinator will be away from September 4 through September 8. Her colleague will answer messages during that period using the same shared mailbox. You can continue using the address already printed on our correspondence.

passages.title: Photography notes for the catalog
heading: To: Studio assistants
From: Nera Dalvik
Subject: Trial photographs
body: The new serving dishes have been photographed at four stations in our studio. At North, we used a pale background with light coming through a large window. At East, the background was dark and the light came through the same window. At South, we used the pale background under ceiling lamps. At West, the background was dark under the ceiling lamps. The dish itself stayed in the same position at every station.

I have sent one image from each station to the catalog editor. We are comparing the photographs before arranging a full day of shooting. The editor has asked us to keep the dish's outline clearly visible without making the glaze look brighter than it really is. There are no people or decorative objects in the trial images.
Please keep all four stations assembled until the editor replies. The large window will be cleaned tomorrow, but that work will take place outside. Nobody needs to move the backgrounds or lamps.

passages.title: Editor's response
body: Thank you for the trial images. The dark backgrounds give the white dishes a clearer outline than the pale ones do. For the main catalog, I would like to use that contrast. Of the two lighting approaches, the window light preserves the subtle gray tones in the glaze better than the ceiling lamps. Please use that lighting approach with the darker background for the full session.

The images also revealed a small mark inside one bowl. Our product team has confirmed that the mark is a removable inventory sticker, not a flaw in the glaze. The sticker should come off before the final photographs are taken. Please do not remove the maker's impression on the underside of the dish, which will appear in a separate detail image. The final catalog will be printed on uncoated paper. I am sending a printed color reference by courier so that your team can compare the finished proofs with the intended appearance. The reference should reach you on Friday.

passages.title: Reading commercial floor-area figures
body: Telvrin Property Surveys provides two figures for office premises. The internal area includes all floor space inside the outer walls, including internal corridors and service rooms. The usable work area excludes those corridors and service rooms. The two measures answer different questions, so neither should be presented without its label.

Tenants planning desk layouts usually begin with the usable work area. Building managers arranging cleaning of the entire interior need the internal area. Our survey drawings show the excluded areas in gray, making it possible to see why the figures differ. Furniture positions do not change either figure; both measures describe the building rather than the tenant's chosen layout. Four suites were surveyed this month. Suite Rowan has an internal area of 160 square meters and a usable work area of 120. Suite Linden measures 150 and 130 respectively. Suite Hazel measures 180 and 140, while Suite Aspen measures 170 and 125. Each suite occupies one floor, and no shared external staircase is included.

The cleaning contractor has asked for a separate list for a quotation covering all interior floors. Please keep that request separate from the desk-layout exercise. The contractor will visit after the design team has prepared its initial sketches. We have not selected a suite or signed a rental agreement yet.

During the visits, I took photographs of the windows and existing floor finishes. These images are in folders carrying the suite names. Our accessibility adviser will review the doorways next Tuesday. Please send the comparison to me by Monday afternoon so I can include it in the adviser’s briefing pack.

passages.title: A hotel tests its new linen
body: The Norevka Hotel is evaluating tablecloths before replacing the stock in its dining rooms. Rather than judging samples straight from their packages, the housekeeping team is washing them repeatedly under the conditions used by the hotel's regular laundry service.
A cloth can look excellent when new but become too small for its intended table after several washes.

The purchasing manager says that consistency is as important as appearance. A tablecloth must extend beyond each edge of a table by the same intended amount. If the drop becomes too short, diners can see the legs and service fittings that the cloth was intended to conceal. The hotel measures each sample after it has dried fully and rested overnight.

Four suppliers provided plain white cloths without decorative borders. Their names were hidden from the staff doing the measurements. The purchasing office alone holds the correspondence linking supplier names to sample codes. That separation allows the housekeeping team to describe the samples without being influenced by previous experience with a vendor.

passages.title: Linen trial measurements
body: The table compares the same edge before and after ten washes. Measurements were taken with the same tape on the same worktable, and no sample was stretched. The staff checked the tape's starting mark before recording the figures.

The staff also recorded observations unrelated to size. L had the softest feel, M dried fastest, N resisted visible creasing best, and P required the least pressing time. These observations will appear in a separate section of the report so readers do not confuse them with the dimensional measurements.

The test table is 150 centimeters long. Cloths are placed with equal overhang at both ends. The staff recorded the total cloth length rather than measuring the overhang directly. All samples will remain in the housekeeping office until the purchasing meeting.

passages.title: Supplier correspondence
heading: To: Housekeeping team
From: Tavin Orle
Subject: Trial suppliers
body: I have checked the original envelopes. Sample L came from Delso Linen, M from Ivarni Cloth, N from Renka Weaving, and P from Solven Textiles. None of the suppliers has seen the other companies' measurements. They were each told only that the hotel was conducting a comparison.

For the first dining room, the manager is prioritizing the smallest reduction in length. The second dining room has not yet set its priorities. The manager also asked for the overhang produced by the cloth from Ivarni on our test table, using the measurements after ten washes.

Please do not return the samples yet. Our restaurant supervisor wants to feel the fabrics in person after tomorrow's breakfast service. She is especially interested in whether diners can move their glasses across the surface easily. I have arranged for her to visit housekeeping at ten thirty, when the measuring table will be clear.

passages.title: Leadership profiles for the annual report
body: Serlavi Foods will feature four employees in the people section of its annual report. The profiles are intended to show the range of decisions made across the company, not to list seniority or length of service. Each person will describe one recent project in ordinary language so that readers outside the business can understand the work.

The editor has assigned the food-development project to the opening profile, the purchasing project to the second, the distribution project to the third, and the financial-planning project to the closing profile. The layout places a portrait beside each story. The profiles will occupy four consecutive pages rather than appearing between the financial statements.

Interviewers should obtain permission to quote each employee and check any figures with the relevant department. They should not send a draft of one person's interview to another employee for approval. Each participant will review only the profile based on their own conversation. Final page proofs will be checked by the report editor.

passages.title: Interview assignments
body: The interview assignments are now confirmed. Dena is interviewing the employee who developed a reduced-salt soup. Orin is meeting the employee who changed how ingredient prices are negotiated. Vela is speaking with the employee who redesigned delivery rounds. Kelm is interviewing the employee who prepared the investment forecast for a new packing line.

The four interviewers have received the same general question list, but each may ask follow-up questions relevant to the project. Sessions are expected to take forty minutes. Audio recordings will be kept in the report team's restricted folder until the participants have checked the written profiles.

Photographs will be taken on a separate day. The photographer needs the interviewers to provide a brief description of each project so the portraits can be made in suitable work settings. A neutral office background is available for any participant whose normal work area is unsuitable.

I have placed the completed drafts in separate folders under the interviewers' names. The participant interviewed by Kelm asked us to replace one numerical value with a range. The participant supplied both endpoints in a separate note. The original figure remains in Kelm's notes, together with the reason for the change. The photographer can work on Wednesday or Thursday next week. Please tell me which day suits your participant. We will send each person an individual appointment rather than asking everyone to wait together. The editor will review the whole section after all four participants have returned their comments.

첫 소개는 식품 개발, 두 번째는 구매, 세 번째는 유통, 마지막은 재무 계획이다. 이야기 옆에 초상 사진을 넣고 재무제표 사이가 아니라 연속 네 면에 싣는다.

passages.title: A wholesaler measures seasonal demand
body: Kelvori Beverage Supply used to compare monthly order totals directly. That approach made short months appear weaker even when customers ordered at the same daily rate. The sales team now reports both the total number of cases ordered and the average per trading day. A month with fewer trading days can have a lower total but a stronger daily rate.

The new report is not a measure of profit. It does not include selling prices, delivery costs, or discounts. Its purpose is to help the warehouse plan the flow of cases through the building. Buyers still examine individual products when deciding what to reorder from manufacturers. The company divides its customer base into four regions. Each region follows the same trading calendar, although their order volumes differ. Seasonal promotions are arranged locally. Managers are asked to describe any unusual local event alongside their numbers rather than assume that every change reflects a general market trend.

passages.title: Regional orders: comparison
body: Cases ordered in April and May, respectively: North region 2,000 and 2,090; East region 1,600 and 1,980; South region 4,000 and 4,400; West region 1,800 and 1,760. These figures include all orders accepted during each month, regardless of the later delivery date.

The figures were prepared by the sales office, not the warehouse. Returned cases are reported separately and are not deducted here. No regional boundary changed between the months, so each pair of figures covers the same customer group.

Local promotion notes: North ran a sports-club offer; East supplied a new outdoor concert series; South distributed sample packs to existing cafés; West tested a smaller minimum order. The notes describe activity rather than estimating how many additional orders it caused.

passages.title: Preparing the warehouse briefing
heading: To: Sales analyst
From: Rina Ostel
Subject: Warehouse briefing
body: April had twenty trading days and May had twenty-two. For tomorrow's briefing, I need the region with the largest increase in cases per trading day, not the largest rise in the monthly total. Please use the comparison prepared by Sales. The warehouse supervisors will use the result when discussing where to assign additional picking staff.

I also need a short note about the region whose daily average stayed exactly the same between April and May. Please identify the local activity listed for that region, but do not claim that the activity caused the result. We have not compared participating customers with customers who did not participate.

The briefing will begin at nine in the warehouse office. Bring the figures on paper because the projector is being used for a safety session elsewhere. I have reserved twenty minutes for the order discussion and another ten for questions from the supervisors. No purchasing decisions will be made during this meeting.

body: 켈보리 음료 도매는 월 총 주문만 비교해 짧은 달이 약하게 보이곤 했다. 이제 총 케이스와 영업일당 평균을 함께 보고한다. 영업일이 적으면 총량이 낮아도 일평균이 높을 수 있다.
이는 이익 지표가 아니며 가격·배송비·할인을 포함하지 않는다. 창고 흐름을 계획하는 목적이다. 제조사 재주문 때는 개별 상품도 살핀다. 고객은 네 지역으로 나누며 같은 영업 달력을 쓰나 물량은 다르다. 판촉은 지역별이다. 모든 변화를 시장 추세로 보지 않도록 특이 지역 사건을 수치와 함께 설명한다.

passages.title: Tactile signs for commercial interiors
body: At Orelva Tactile Works, we produce signs that can be read by touch as well as by sight. Raised lettering helps visitors recognize room names, while a separate line of tactile dots provides the same information in another reading system. The two elements are prepared independently and checked before they are mounted on a backing plate.

Our four sample plates demonstrate different finishes rather than different messages. Plate Ash has a brushed metal backing and square corners. Plate Elm has a brushed metal backing and rounded corners. Plate Pine has a smooth resin backing and square corners. Plate Yew has a smooth resin backing and rounded corners. Each sample says Meeting Room and includes the corresponding tactile dots.

Customers receive the sample box by courier and may keep it for one week. Please examine the surface under the actual corridor lighting. The sample box contains a return sleeve and a form for reporting any damaged pieces.
Installation is quoted separately after a technician has seen the intended walls.

passages.title: Comments on the sample signs
heading: To: Orelva Tactile Works
From: Leni Mavren
Subject: Sample feedback
body: Our accessibility group examined the box yesterday. Everyone could distinguish the raised elements clearly on all four plates. The facilities team prefers metal to resin because the existing door furniture has a similar finish. The group also prefers curved edges for the signs beside the narrow corridor, where people sometimes brush against the wall.

Please prepare a quotation for twenty signs in the finish that combines those preferences. The room names will differ, and I will send the complete list after our department managers check the spelling. We do not need additional samples with the final room names at this stage. The box is on my desk and will be collected by our courier tomorrow. One corner of the outer carton was crushed when it arrived, but every sample inside was intact. I have included a photograph of the carton on the return form. A technician can visit us on Tuesday morning.

passagesKo.title: 상업 공간용 촉각 표지
body: 오렐바 촉각 표지는 눈과 손으로 읽는 표지를 만든다. 돌출 글자와 같은 정보를 나타내는 별도 한 줄의 촉각 점들을 각각 제작·검사해 바탕판에 부착한다.
네 표본은 메시지 대신 마감을 비교한다. Ash는 브러시 금속·각진 모서리, Elm은 브러시 금속·둥근 모서리, Pine은 매끈한 수지·각진 모서리, Yew는 매끈한 수지·둥근 모서리다. 모두 Meeting Room과 해당 촉각 점이 있다.

설치는 기술자의 벽 확인 후 별도 견적이다.

passages.title: From freezer to pastry counter
body: Derveni Bakehouse supplies unbaked pastry pieces to its café branches. Before baking, each kind spends a specified time thawing and then a separate time rising. These stages cannot overlap. Oven time begins only when both have finished, and pastries must cool for ten minutes after leaving the oven before being placed on the counter.

The preparation card lists four kinds. Apricot twists require twenty minutes of thawing, thirty of rising, and twenty of baking. Almond knots require thirty, forty, and twenty respectively. Cocoa rolls require twenty, fifty, and twenty. Lemon spirals require forty, thirty, and twenty. The cooling period is the same for all four.

Branches may begin preparation at different times, but the sequence remains unchanged. Staff should write the actual start time on the tray card. If a customer asks when a pastry will be ready, staff can then calculate the counter time from that entry rather than guess from the appearance of the dough. Empty trays should be washed away from the preparation bench.

passages.title: Morning preparation notes
heading: To: Counter team
From: Neli Orvan
Subject: Morning trays
body: The trays were taken out of the freezer at the following times today: apricot twists at 7:10, almond knots at 6:50, cocoa rolls at 7:00, and lemon spirals at 7:20. Each tray began thawing immediately. We followed the preparation card exactly and moved every tray to the next stage without delay. The oven has separate compartments, so trays did not have to wait for one another.

Our first office delivery is being collected at 8:35. The driver will collect only pastries that have completed cooling by then. He will return later for the remaining trays. I have placed separate delivery labels beside the counter so the two collections can be packed independently. The almond tray contains one extra piece for staff tasting. Please keep that piece separate from the customer's order after cooling. The customer has already paid for the delivery, and the driver has the address. Only the final tray list remains to be added to his collection sheet.

passagesKo.title: 냉동고에서 판매대까지
body: 데르베니 제과는 지점에 굽지 않은 냉동 생지를 보낸다. 해동과 발효는 별도이며 겹칠 수 없다. 둘 다 끝난 뒤 굽고 오븐에서 나온 후10분 식혀야 판매대에 놓는다.
살구 트위스트는 해동20·발효30·굽기20분, 아몬드 매듭은30·40·20, 코코아 롤은20·50·20, 레몬 나선은40·30·20분이다. 식힘은 모두 같다.
지점별 시작 시각은 달라도 순서는 같다. 트레이 카드에 실제 시작을 써 두면 고객에게 반죽 모양으로 추측하지 않고 판매 가능 시각을 계산해 줄 수 있다. 빈 트레이는 준비대와 떨어진 곳에서 씻는다.

passages.title: Cargo bicycles reach the business district
body: Osvarel Couriers has opened a small bicycle depot near the central business district. Vans bring parcels to the depot in the morning, and riders complete the last part of each journey. The arrangement allows the company to use narrow streets where a van would have difficulty finding a stopping place. Heavy freight still travels directly by van.

The service began with four routes, named after the streets containing most of their stops. Route Copper serves the printing businesses. Route Silver serves the legal offices. Route Brass serves the clothing wholesalers. Route Tin serves the design studios. These route names appear on dispatch records rather than on customers' address labels. Each rider checks the contents of a sealed dispatch bag against a list before leaving. The rider obtains a signature at every completed delivery. A parcel that cannot be handed over returns to the depot; it is not left outside a closed business. Customers receive a message after the depot has entered the rider's return notes.

passages.title: Wednesday rider allocation
body: Wednesday assignments: Ilen rides Copper, Varo rides Silver, Nesa rides Brass, and Tovin rides Tin. The bicycles have been checked, and every rider has a charged handheld device. The route assignments apply to the morning round only; afternoon rounds will be assigned after the returned parcels have been sorted.

The dispatcher gave each rider a numbered bag and a separate list of stops. Riders should report changes to the dispatcher rather than exchange bags among themselves. This keeps the dispatch record aligned with the person responsible for collecting signatures. Rain covers are available beside the depot door.

The morning riders left at 9:15. The depot expects them back by noon, but a rider may return earlier after completing all listed stops. Bicycles should be parked in their marked bays so the mechanic can inspect them before the afternoon departures.

passages.title: Morning round outcomes
heading: To: Customer desk
From: Eri Malven
Subject: Morning round outcomes
body: Ilen completed every stop and returned an empty bag. Varo brought one parcel back because the recipient's office was locked. Nesa completed all but one delivery; the person at that address said the business had moved, and the parcel is back here. Tovin obtained signatures at all addresses and returned at 11:20.

Please send the appropriate customer messages once these notes have been entered. The parcel from the locked office has a valid address on the dispatch list; the rider saw the company name beside the door. The parcel from the relocated business has the old address printed on its label. Both parcels are on the returns shelf, separated from tomorrow's incoming work.

The depot mechanic found no damage on the returned bicycles. One rain cover was wet and is hanging beside the sink. I have placed all signed delivery lists in the dispatch drawer. The afternoon dispatcher can use those lists when answering customer questions about this morning's completed deliveries.

passagesKo.title: 업무 지구의 화물 자전거
body: 오스바렐 택배는 중심 업무 지구 근처 자전거 거점을 열었다. 아침에 밴이 소포를 옮기면 자전거가 마지막 구간을 담당한다. 밴 정차가 어려운 좁은 거리를 이용하며 무거운 화물은 밴으로 직접 간다.

네 경로는 주요 정차 거리 이름을 쓴다. Copper는 인쇄업체, Silver는 법률 사무실, Brass는 의류 도매상, Tin은 디자인실이다. 고객 주소 라벨이 아니라 배차 기록에 표시한다. 출발 전 봉인 가방 내용물을 목록과 대조하며 전달 때 서명을 받는다. 전달하지 못하면 닫힌 업체 밖에 두지 않고 거점으로 반송한다. 반송 메모가 입력되면 고객에게 메시지가 간다.

body: 수요일 오전 배정은 Ilen-Copper, Varo-Silver, Nesa-Brass, Tovin-Tin이다. 자전거와 충전 기기를 점검했다. 오후는 반송 소포 분류 후 다시 배정한다.
각자 번호 가방과 별도 정차 목록을 받았다. 가방을 서로 바꾸지 말고 배차원에게 변경을 알려 서명 수집 책임자와 기록이 맞게 한다. 문 옆에 빗물 덮개가 있다.

passages.title: Reading kiln witness pieces
body: Velori Ceramics places a small witness piece beside each shelf of cups before firing. These pieces are made from a material that bends progressively as it receives heat. They provide evidence about the combined effect of temperature and time in that part of the kiln. A wall-mounted thermometer, by contrast, reports conditions at its own location at a particular moment.

For this cup design, the technical team classifies a witness piece standing upright as insufficient firing, one bent halfway as the target result, and one lying flat as excessive firing. This interpretation applies to the witness material used in this trial. It is not a general instruction for other materials or products.

Inspectors record the witness result before the cups are placed in shipping cartons. The witness pieces remain beside their shelf labels for comparison. The trial also includes visual checks of the glaze, but those checks are recorded separately. The production manager will consider both sources before deciding whether to change the firing schedule.

passages.title: Trial shelf record
body: Each order occupied one shelf, and none was moved during firing. Inspectors recorded the shapes shown in the table before consulting the technical team's interpretation. The order names identify customer batches rather than different cup models.

The cups on all shelves had the same dimensions and glaze recipe. Staff loaded the kiln in the afternoon and unloaded it the next morning after cooling. The record was completed before any cups were packed for dispatch. The shelf labels remained visible throughout the inspection.

A separate note records cosmetic observations: Brin had a consistent surface, Cavo showed a darker edge, Deli had a slightly rough base, and Fenn had one small glaze drip. These comments are descriptions only; the inspector did not assign a final acceptance decision to any order.

body: Please identify which order's witness result indicates insufficient firing. I want to compare that shelf's position with the air-circulation drawing before the next trial. The drawing is in the technical folder, but it has not yet been added to the inspection packet.

For the customer discussion, note that order Brin is for the café at Relsa House, Cavo for the dining room at Nerin Court, Deli for the breakfast room at Varo Lodge, and Fenn for the lounge at Elsi Hall. These are the customers' descriptions of the rooms, not separate product specifications. All four orders use the same cup design. The packing team has counted the cups and confirmed that the quantities match the order sheets. They have not sealed the cartons. Please leave the witness pieces on the inspection bench until I have compared them in person. I will be back at the factory after my supplier visit on Thursday afternoon.

passages.title: Broken-needle investigation
body: The sewing room at Dalvori Workwear uses a numbered pouch system when a machine needle breaks. Operators place the recovered pieces in a pouch and record the machine and time. The supervisor compares the recovered pieces with an intact needle of the same model. The comparison concerns the complete physical shape, not just the number of pieces found.

If the pieces reconstruct the entire needle, the incident is marked complete. If a section remains unaccounted for, the affected garments stay in a separate holding area while the search continues. A needle can break into two large pieces or several smaller ones, so a higher piece count does not by itself mean a better recovery. A technician examines the machine after every breakage, even when all fragments have been found. The sewing supervisor, rather than the technician, records the garment decision. The incident folder includes the operator's account and a photograph of the reconstructed needle so that later reviewers can see the basis of that decision.

passages.title: Recovery observations
body: Pouch R contains two fragments that form the full outline of the reference needle when joined. Pouch S contains four fragments, but the pointed end is absent. Pouch T contains three fragments that reconstruct the full outline. Pouch U contains five fragments, with a section of the shaft absent. Each comparison used the correct reference model.

The photographs were taken on a white measuring card. The reference needle appears beside the recovered pieces in every photograph, but it was not placed inside the recovery pouch. Staff counted only the recovered fragments, so the reference is not included in any of the totals above.

The supervisor has signed the observation sheet. A second employee checked the pouch numbers against the photographs. The images are stored in the incident folder in the same order as the pouches, and no fragment was transferred from one pouch to another during the comparison.

body: The production sheets link pouch R to the navy jackets, S to the green aprons, T to the gray trousers, and U to the cream shirts. Each group was sewn on a different machine. The garments are still labeled with their production references, and no groups have been mixed.

The technician has examined all four machines and replaced their needles. He found no additional fragments inside the machine housings. His service notes are attached. The sewing supervisor has the observation sheet and will enter the incident statuses after reviewing the photographs.

The customer service team has asked which groups remain in the holding area. They are preparing a factual update for the customers, without promising a dispatch date. Please give them the garment descriptions rather than the pouch letters, since the customers do not have access to our internal recovery records. The completed production counts are already available in their order system.

passagesKo.title: 부러진 바늘 조사
body: 달보리 작업복 재봉실은 바늘 파손 시 번호 주머니를 쓴다. 작업자는 회수 조각과 기계·시간을 기록하고 감독자는 같은 모델의 온전한 바늘과 형태를 비교한다. 단순 조각 수가 아닌 전체 물리적 형태를 본다.

전체가 복원되면 사건을 완료로 표시한다. 일부가 없으면 의류를 별도 보류 구역에 두고 찾는다. 두 큰 조각 또는 여러 작은 조각으로 부러질 수 있어 조각 수가 많다고 더 잘 회수한 것은 아니다. 모든 파손 후 기술자가 기계를 살피지만 의류 결정은 재봉 감독자가 기록한다. 작업자 진술과 복원 사진을 사건 폴더에 넣어 추후 검토자가 판단 근거를 볼 수 있게 한다.

body: R의 두 조각은 연결하면 전체 형태를 만들고 S의 네 조각은 뾰족한 끝이 없다. T의 세 조각은 전체를 복원하고 U의 다섯 조각은 몸통 일부가 없다. 모두 맞는 기준 모델을 썼다.
흰 측정 카드 위에서 사진을 찍었다. 기준 바늘은 옆에 있지만 회수 주머니에 넣지 않았고 조각 수에도 포함하지 않았다.
감독자가 서명했고 다른 직원이 주머니 번호와 사진을 대조했다. 사건 폴더의 사진 순서는 주머니와 같으며 비교 중 조각을 서로 옮기지 않았다.

passages.title: Comparing pantry pack prices
body: Nerova Pantry's wholesale catalog shows both a package price and a price per one hundred grams. The package price is the amount paid for the whole container. The unit price allows customers to compare containers of different sizes. A lower package price does not always mean that the contents are cheaper by weight.

This week's plain oat products have the following package sizes and prices: Mill bag, 500 grams for $3.00; Field bag, 750 grams for $4.20; Hearth bag, 1,000 grams for $5.40; Brook bag, 400 grams for $2.60. All contain the same grade of plain oats and are sold without an additional delivery charge on the company's regular route.

The bags have different outer designs because they were prepared for different wholesale customers. Those designs do not indicate differences in ingredients. Customers may order any combination of bags. The catalog team can provide ingredient sheets for each product, and the warehouse records the batch number on the dispatch note.

heading: To: Purchasing assistant

Subject: Breakfast supplies

Within that limit, please choose the lowest cost for an equal weight of oats. Cupboard space is sufficient, and we do not need to compare brands or recipes. The pantry team has approved the grade described in the catalog.

For our first order, buy six kilograms of the selected product. Please use whole bags only. The team has enough oats for the rest of this week, so the regular delivery route is fine. There is no need to arrange an extra vehicle or pay for an urgent collection. Our kitchen assistant will check the dispatch note when the bags arrive. I would like the ingredient sheets filed beside the breakfast menu because employees sometimes ask about the products we use. The cupboard has been cleaned, and new shelf labels are ready. Please send me the final order quantity before you submit it.

passages.title: Reading cumulative donation totals
body: The employee giving dashboard at Solvren Engineering displays cumulative totals for the current campaign. The number beside a month includes that month's gifts plus all earlier gifts in the same campaign. It is not the amount collected during that month alone. To find a single month's contribution, subtract the preceding month's cumulative total.

The campaign supports four local projects, each identified by a letter on the internal dashboard. Project A funds school instruments, B supports coastal habitat work, C funds reading recordings, and D supports a community kitchen. The public campaign leaflet uses the full project descriptions rather than the internal letters. Employees choose the project they wish to support when submitting a gift. The company does not move gifts between projects. Payroll deductions and direct transfers are combined in the dashboard once received. The communications team updates the public leaflet after Finance checks the monthly figures, but the internal dashboard is available earlier.

body: The dashboard snapshots are attached in text form. At the end of March, the totals were A $1,200, B $900, C $1,500, and D $800. At the end of April, they were A $1,700, B $1,600, C $1,900, and D $1,400. The campaign began in February and all figures are in dollars.

For the next newsletter, please identify the project that received the largest amount during April alone. I would also like the April amount for the project supporting a community kitchen. Please use full project descriptions in the newsletter, as most readers have not seen the internal dashboard.

The newsletter goes to the printer on Thursday. Finance has checked these snapshots, so no further confirmation of the figures is needed. The editor will add a photograph supplied by one of the participating organizations. We have permission to use that photograph in the printed newsletter and in the staff portal version.

passages.title: Captioned performances at the Lervani Stage
body: The Lervani Stage offers live captions at selected performances. A caption operator follows the actors and sends the spoken words to screens beside the stage. The screens also identify important sounds that affect the story. Captions are not a translation into another language; they reproduce the performance language for people who prefer to read the dialogue.

Captioned dates are chosen separately for each production. The autumn program includes Glass Harbor, a drama about a family business; The Last Orchard, a musical; Paper Roads, a comedy about traveling salespeople; and Evening Ledger, a mystery set in a hotel. All four productions run for several weeks.

The box office can advise on seats with a clear view of both stage and caption screens. Customers should mention their interest in captions when booking rather than assume every performance uses them. A demonstration of the screens is available in the foyer before each captioned performance. Staff can show how the text changes without revealing any of the story.

passages.title: Autumn caption calendar
body: The captioned performances are: Glass Harbor, October 6 at 19:00; The Last Orchard, October 12 at 14:00; Paper Roads, October 19 at 19:00; Evening Ledger, October 26 at 14:00. These times refer to the start of the performance. The foyer demonstration begins thirty minutes earlier on each date.

The screen positions are checked during the afternoon technical rehearsal. Caption operators receive the current script, but they follow the live performance rather than run a fixed-speed recording. If an actor pauses longer than expected, the operator can wait before displaying the next line.

Tickets for these performances are sold through the regular box office. Customers receive a confirmation naming the production and date. The confirmation does not list the foyer demonstration separately, because it is included for anyone attending the performance. Large-print program notes can be collected from the information counter.

passagesKo.title: 레르바니 극장의 자막 공연
body: 레르바니 극장은 일부 공연에서 실시간 자막을 제공한다. 운영자가 배우를 따라 대사와 이야기 관련 주요 소리를 무대 옆 화면에 보낸다. 다른 언어 번역이 아니라 공연 언어를 읽고 싶은 사람용이다.
가을 Glass Harbor는 가족 사업 드라마, The Last Orchard는 뮤지컬, Paper Roads는 순회 영업사원 코미디, Evening Ledger는 호텔 미스터리다. 각각 여러 주 공연하며 자막일은 별도다.

passages.title: Comparing overseas quotations
body: For its training exercise, the purchasing team at Velsori Components converts overseas quotations into a fictional home currency called the lorn. The exercise uses fixed conversion rates printed on a separate worksheet. These are classroom figures, not current market rates. The purpose is to compare quotations expressed in different currencies without confusing the quoted amount with the cost in lorns.

For this exercise, multiply the foreign-currency amount by the listed number of lorns per unit. Delivery charges already included in a quotation should not be added again. All four suppliers are offering the same number of identical practice items, so a separate per-item calculation is unnecessary. The facilitator asks participants to keep their calculation notes. The discussion afterward focuses on how an apparently smaller foreign-currency number can produce a larger converted cost. Supplier quality and payment terms are outside this exercise; participants should not assume that the lowest converted cost would always decide a real purchasing contract.

passages.title: Practice quotation worksheet
body: The table supplies the fictional conversion rates and quotations for this exercise. The same rates apply to every participant. Do not look up external currency information; no real currency or market movement is involved in the exercise.

Each quotation includes delivery and covers fifty identical practice units. The suppliers' names are labels for the exercise and do not refer to real companies. No taxes or additional fees need to be added to the figures in the table.

The worksheet includes space for recording the original amount, the multiplication used, and the converted result. Participants should complete all four rows before ranking them. A spare copy is available at the front desk for anyone who wants to redo the arithmetic during the group discussion.

passages.title: Preparing the exercise discussion
heading: To: Training assistant
From: Eren Malvi
Subject: Exercise discussion
body: Four participants have chosen different quotations to present. Leni will explain Anvel's, Orta will explain Brelta's, Mavin will explain Corven's, and Tesa will explain Delsa's. Each participant should show the arithmetic, not simply read the final figure aloud.

Please invite the person whose quotation produces the lowest cost in lorns to speak first. After that, invite the person presenting the second-lowest quotation. The other two can speak in either order. We have not asked participants to negotiate with the fictional suppliers or change any quoted amounts.

I have reserved the smaller training room for forty-five minutes. The wall board is available, and there are markers in the drawer. Please leave the conversion worksheet visible throughout the discussion so people can check one another's calculations. At the end, collect the completed sheets for the facilitator's review, but let participants keep their personal notes.

passages.title: Understanding cartridge yield estimates
body: Tervali Office Ink expresses its cartridge estimates in standard-page equivalents. For this product, one standard page has ink covering five percent of its surface. A page with ten percent coverage counts as two standard pages, while a page with fifteen percent counts as three. The estimate is a planning tool; it does not promise an exact number of physical sheets for every document.

Customers comparing cartridge options should therefore consider what they print. A short letter and a densely illustrated flyer can use very different quantities of ink even when they use the same paper size. Blank areas do not consume ink simply because they pass through the printer.

The current cartridge range contains four sizes: Leaf is rated for 600 standard pages, Stem for 900, Branch for 1,200, and Crown for 1,800. All are compatible with the same printer. The cartridge name describes its capacity option, not a difference in ink color or paper compatibility. Empty cartridges can be returned in the supplied envelope.

passages.title: Print jobs planned for the induction pack
body: The communications team has prepared four jobs. Welcome letters require 200 physical sheets at five percent coverage. Site maps require 150 sheets at ten percent. Product diagrams require 100 sheets at fifteen percent. Contact lists require 200 sheets at ten percent. All jobs use one printed side per sheet.

These figures come from the approved print files. No additional copies are planned, and none of the pages will be printed on the reverse. The office printer uses the cartridge family described in the supplier's capacity guide. For planning purposes, assume that the coverage estimate applies exactly and that no ink is used for other operations. The files are in separate folders so staff can stop after completing a job. A label on each folder states the physical-sheet quantity. Please do not confuse that label with the supplier's standard-page measure. The final packs will be assembled by the training team after printing.

The operator has already tested the paper feed with blank sheets. She will begin with the welcome letters, continue with the maps and diagrams, and finish with the contact lists. The test used no ink and none of the new cartridges has been installed. The printer is otherwise ready.

Please tell me the total standard-page requirement as well as the cartridge name. I will add both to our supplies record so the next coordinator understands the choice. The empty-cartridge envelope is in the same cupboard. After the packs are assembled, the training team will check that each includes all four documents.

passages.title: Day visits at the Velrani Pet Hotel
body: The Velrani Pet Hotel gives owners a written summary after each trial day. The summary describes meals, rest periods, and the activities the animal joined. Staff record observations rather than assigning a general personality label. An animal that rests quietly on its first visit may behave differently after becoming familiar with the building.

Four activity areas are used during the trial. Area K is an outdoor grass enclosure, Area L is an indoor play space, Area M is a quiet resting area, and Area N is a covered exercise path. Staff move animals between areas individually, and the same animal may use several areas during one visit. Owners receive a timetable showing where their animal spent each part of the day. They can discuss that timetable with the employee who supervised the visit. The hotel does not combine animals from different households during a first trial day. Food brought from home is kept in a labeled container and returned if unused.

passages.title: Pella's trial-day summary
heading: To: Pella's owner
From: Nira Selvo
Subject: Trial-day summary
body: Pella arrived at nine and spent the first hour in Area L with her supervising employee. From ten until eleven she was in Area K. After her meal, she rested in Area M until one thirty. She then spent half an hour in Area N before returning to Area L for the rest of the visit.

She ate most of the food you supplied. The unused portion is in the original labeled container, which we returned with her bag. She approached the employee readily during play but preferred to rest alone after eating. These are observations from today rather than predictions about future visits.

Your next trial booking is for Thursday. Please bring the same bag so we can keep her belongings together. The supervising employee will be available at collection time to discuss today's timetable and answer questions about how the areas are used. We have attached the attendance record for your own files.

Area K는 야외 잔디 울타리, Area L은 실내 놀이 공간, Area M는 조용한 휴식 공간, Area N는 지붕 있는 운동로다. 개별적으로 이동하며 하루 여러 곳을 쓸 수 있다. 보호자는 시간표를 받고 담당자와 논의할 수 있다. 첫 방문에는 다른 가정 동물과 섞지 않는다. 집에서 가져온 사료는 라벨 용기에 보관하고 남으면 돌려준다.

passages.title: Who creates a book jacket?
body: At Nolvari Press, several specialists contribute to a book jacket. An illustrator creates the image, a designer arranges the image and text, a letterer draws any custom title lettering, and a production specialist prepares the final file for printing. One person may perform several roles, but credits identify the actual contribution rather than merely naming a team.

The new travel essay collection, Quiet Crossings, has a jacket produced by four people. Mera Voss supplied the river illustration. Tavin Rel arranged the illustration, title, and author name. Olin Sera drew the title characters by hand. Nela Fenn checked color separations and prepared the print-ready file. The author's own photographs appear inside the book, not on the jacket.

The press now includes detailed jacket credits on its website because readers often ask who made a particular visual element. The credits also help booksellers direct requests for permissions or interviews. They do not change ownership arrangements, which are set out in separate agreements. A printed copy of the credits appears beside the book's publication information.

passages.title: A bookseller's display idea
heading: To: Nolvari Press
From: Reni Oskel
Subject: Book display proposal
body: Our shop is planning a small display about the making of Quiet Crossings. Several customers noticed the hand-drawn title and asked how the shapes were developed. We would like to invite the person responsible for that element to explain the process in a short recorded interview. The recording would play beside the display, with headphones for visitors.

We would also like to show a sketch from the person who created the river image. A rough early version would be useful because it would let customers compare the starting point with the finished jacket. We are not asking for the author's interior photographs or the file used by the printer. Please put us in touch with the two contributors so we can discuss availability and permission directly. The display is planned for next month, but the exact opening date remains flexible. Our events assistant will handle the interview arrangements, and our display manager will take care of the physical materials.

passages.title: Finding a bicycle line's limiting stage
body: Elvori Cycles assembles each bicycle through four stages: frame preparation, wheel fitting, brake adjustment, and final inspection. A bicycle must pass through them in that order. The production team is studying the maximum number of completed bicycles the line can produce in an hour when the stages work continuously.

The slowest stage determines the line's sustained hourly capacity. Faster stages may create a temporary queue, but they cannot make completed bicycles pass through a slower stage more quickly. The study assumes that material is always available and that no bicycle needs to repeat a stage. Startup time and breaks are excluded from the comparison. The company is considering extra staffing at one stage. Its managers want to distinguish an improvement at a single workstation from an improvement in the output of the whole line. They will use the trial figures to discuss that distinction before buying equipment. The figures are intended for planning, not for evaluating individual employees' performance.

passages.title: Hourly capacity trial
body: Current capacities are frame preparation 18 bicycles, wheel fitting 12, brake adjustment 15, and final inspection 20 per hour. These values were measured over continuous runs using the same bicycle model. Each stage had the normal tools and its usual working space.

A second worker can be added to wheel fitting without changing the layout. In a separate test, that arrangement raised wheel fitting to 24 bicycles per hour. The capacities of the other three stages were not changed during that test. A separate alternative put the extra worker at brake adjustment, raising that stage to 30 bicycles per hour while all other stages retained their current capacities.

Observers counted bicycles only when they completed a stage. Partly finished work was recorded in a separate notebook and is not included in the hourly figures. The trial team photographed the workstation layouts so the same arrangements can be reproduced for a later test. The production manager has copies of both the figures and photographs.

passages.title: Planning the afternoon demonstration
heading: To: Demonstration guide
From: Lera Varn
Subject: Afternoon production demonstration
body: For the afternoon demonstration, we will use the arrangement with the extra worker at wheel fitting. The frame, brake, and inspection teams will keep their normal arrangements. We will run long enough for the line to reach a steady flow and then count completed bicycles for one hour.

Please tell the visitors which stage will limit the completed output under this arrangement. Also show the increase in the line's sustained hourly capacity compared with the current arrangement. They have seen the wheel-fitting improvement but have not yet discussed what happens to the full line.

The visitors are purchasing managers from our distributors. They will stand in the marked observation area rather than walk between workstations. We have provided a printed sequence diagram, and a guide will explain the terms before the run begins. The question period will take place afterward in the sales room, where the trial figures can be displayed on a large screen.

passages.title: Continuity notes for a company film
body: The short film for Nesvori Instruments follows a customer order through four scenes. Although the story unfolds in one morning, the scenes will be filmed on different days. Objects that appear in consecutive scenes must look consistent so viewers do not notice the change in filming dates.

In Scene One, a red folder sits on the left side of the reception desk. In Scene Two, the same folder is carried into the planning room with a white label on its front. In Scene Three, a technician opens that folder in the testing room beside a blue sample case. In Scene Four, the customer receives the blue case at the dispatch counter. The folder remains with the technician.

The continuity assistant photographs the objects after each setup. These images are reference material for later filming, not publicity photographs. If a replacement object is used, the assistant must compare its visible features with the reference image before the cameras run. The director will decide whether any noticeable difference requires an earlier shot to be repeated.

passages.title: Filming allocation
body: Scene One is assigned to team Alder on Monday. Scene Two is assigned to team Birch on Wednesday. Scene Three is assigned to team Cedar on Tuesday. Scene Four is assigned to team Willow on Thursday. The dates reflect room availability, not the sequence of the story.

Each team receives only the pages relevant to its own scene. The production coordinator keeps the full sequence and distributes continuity photographs as soon as they are available. Team members should use the scene number when labeling their images rather than just the filming date.

The red folder and blue case belong to the prop department. They are checked out separately and returned at the end of each filming day. The desk and planning-room furniture remain in their normal locations. Staff working nearby have been told when the cameras will be in their rooms so they can avoid entering a shot.

The replacement is the same red shade and size as the original but has no label on its front. The original photographs are in the continuity folder.

Tuesday's team finished its scene before the damage occurred. No further shots are planned with that team. Wednesday's team has collected the replacement folder, while Thursday's team has reserved the blue case. The prop department has blank white labels and can provide one if requested. Please pass these facts to the continuity assistant. The damaged cover has been kept in a separate envelope, and the undamaged contents of the folder are in the replacement. The receptionist has also confirmed that the desk will be available on Thursday. The production coordinator will circulate the next day's call sheet this afternoon.

passages.title: Reading the hotel performance sheet
body: The management exercise at Orvani Lodging compares four hotels using occupied room-nights. One room occupied for three nights counts as three room-nights, whether one person or two people stay in it. The measure is different from the number of guests and from the number of separate bookings.

Average room revenue is calculated by dividing room revenue by occupied room-nights. For this exercise, the revenue figure excludes meals, parking, and other extras. This makes the comparison about accommodation alone. The exercise does not compare profit because operating costs have not been supplied.

All figures concern the same seven-night period. The training facilitator asks participants to calculate each property's average before discussing the results. A hotel can have the highest room revenue without having the highest average per occupied room-night. The team should explain that distinction in ordinary language when presenting the figures to colleagues outside Finance.

passages.title: Training data: four properties
body: The data sheet identifies properties by code. Occupied room-night totals have already been checked against nightly room registers. Revenue was copied from the accommodation ledger for the same dates. Both columns describe completed activity rather than future reservations.

No food or parking revenue is included. Canceled reservations are excluded because they produced no occupied room-nights in this period. The figures are complete for the seven nights and contain no estimate for later arrivals. Each property uses the same definition supplied in the exercise notice. The worksheet leaves space for participants to write the calculated average and then rank the properties. The facilitator will collect the rankings before displaying the property names. This allows participants to make their numerical comparison without relying on their previous impression of a particular hotel.

passages.title: Names for the training presentation
heading: To: Training facilitator
From: Eni Varel
Subject: Property names
body: Here is the code list for the presentation: H is the Alder Court, J is the Linden House, K is the Hazel Lodge, and M is the Aspen Inn. The names were withheld only for the first calculation round. They can appear in the discussion slides afterward.

Please open the discussion with the hotel that has the highest average room revenue per occupied room-night. Then identify the hotel with the greatest total room revenue, so participants can see whether the two measures lead to the same property. Use the accommodation-only figures on the training sheet.

The property managers will not attend the session. This is an exercise for new sales coordinators, not a ranking of manager performance. The facilitator will ask one participant to explain the room-night measure using a simple stay example. Please leave enough time for that explanation before moving on to the numerical comparison. Printed copies of the slides will be available for everyone to take away.
